methodologyNotes: Roster covers fourteen record cleaning machines spanning manual immersion washers, motorized vacuum RCMs, and ultrasonic systems, verified 2026-08-12 primarily against manufacturer/brand pages (Pro-Ject, Okki Nokki, HumminGuru, VPI, Nitty Gritty, Clearaudio, Degritter, Spin-Clean, Kirmuss Audio, Audio Desk Systeme, iSonic, HiFi GEM) where reachable, and against authorized-dealer product pages (Audio Advisor, Turntable Lab, Music Direct, Acoustic Sounds, Upscale Audio) where the manufacturer's own site did not publish consumer pricing or full specs (a common pattern in high-end audio, which sells through dealer networks). Two seed entries required correction/clarification rather than a straight lookup: (1) "Gem Dandy" is not a vacuum or ultrasonic RCM but a no-contact hydraulic (tap-water-jet) LP washer, invented by George E. Merrill and still sold today by HiFi GEM as the "Hydraulic LP Cleaning Apparatus Mk II" (hifigem.com); price ($119) is a directly-documented figure from a detailed 6moons review of the current product since HiFi GEM's own page does not display a list price, and priceNote flags that it may not reflect current pricing. (2) "Moth" (the Moth Mk2 vacuum RCM, UK-made, sold factory-built or as a DIY kit) is discontinued with no current manufacturer storefront found; no reliable successor/rebrand could be confirmed live in this pass, so it is retained as a legacy product with priceUsd left null and priceNote citing the GBP 275-280 secondhand range seen on UK hi-fi forums (theartofsound.net), rather than guessing a current USD price. Fields left null throughout (rather than estimated) wherever a source did not explicitly publish that figure — this is common for motor wattage on vacuum RCMs (several manufacturers state only that a machine uses "the same vacuum motor" as a sibling model, or omit the figure entirely) and for cycle time/tank capacity on machines marketed as fully automatic without a published duration. accessedAt 2026-08-12 throughout.

products.name: Pro-Ject VC-S3 Premium Record Cleaning Vacuum Machine
products.priceNote: Audio Advisor US retail price; Pro-Ject's own site (project-audio.com) routes buyers to "Find a Dealer" and does not display consumer pricing

specs.cycle_time: Dries within 2 platter rotations at 30 RPM
specs.drying_method: Vacuum suction wand on a tonearm-style pickup arm

products.provenance: Audio Advisor's listing confirms $699 price, 30 RPM cleaning speed, 2.5 L (85 oz) fluid capacity, 2-rotation dry time, magnetic clamp system, and 17.6 lb weight. Pro-Ject's own product page corroborates the wet-clean-then-vacuum-dry process and the "Wash it 2" eco-friendly fluid, but neither source publishes a motor wattage or noise-level figure, so both are left null rather than assumed.

products.name: Okki Nokki ONE DV Record Cleaning Machine
products.priceNote: Turntable Lab US retail price; Okki Nokki (Netherlands) sells through a dealer network and does not publish consumer pricing directly

specs.tank_capacity: Integrated waste-fluid reservoir with level indicator (numeric capacity not published)
specs.drying_method: Configurable unibody vacuum arm and built-in hose, fits 7", 10", and 12" records

products.provenance: Turntable Lab's product page confirms $749 price, aluminum unibody/ABS construction, configurable vacuum arm for all three common record sizes, integrated reservoir with level indicator, 50ml cleaning fluid concentrate, goat-hair brush, stainless steel clamp, extra 7" platter, and 2-year warranty. The page markets it as "the quietest vacuum RCM on the market" but gives no numeric dB figure, and no motor wattage, cycle-time, or tank-volume figure was published on this or the Okki Nokki manufacturer page, so those fields are left null.

products.name: HumminGuru Ultrasonic Vinyl Record Cleaner

specs.cycle_time: 2 or 5 min clean cycle + 5 or 10 min dry cycle (auto quick-clean or deep-clean modes)
specs.drying_method: Built-in fan with air filter that separates dust during cleaning and drying

products.provenance: Turntable Lab's product page fully specifies the HumminGuru: 40 kHz ultrasonic frequency, 350 ml removable tank, 45 W power draw, 60-70 dB noise level, 2/5-minute clean settings with 5/10-minute dry settings (or combined auto quick/deep modes), filtered-air drying, native 12" compatibility with optional 7"/10" adapters, and $599.99 price. Manufacturer requires distilled water only.

products.name: VPI HW-16.5 Record Cleaning Machine
products.priceNote: Music Direct / Acoustic Sounds US retail price (VPI's own site routes to dealers, MSRP corroborated identically at both retailers)

specs.drying_method: Vacuum pickup tube, adjustable for record thickness, into a stainless-steel internal fluid-collection system

Motor power in watts is never stated by either source (only amperage), so it is left null rather than computed by assumption; reservoir capacity in liters/oz is likewise not published, so tank_capacity is null.

products.name: Nitty Gritty Model 1.0 Record Cleaning Machine
products.priceNote: Nitty Gritty Inc. list price; commonly discounted to ~$524 (Elusive Disc)

specs.cleaning_method: Vacuum (fully manual: hand-applied fluid, hand-brushed, hand-rotated platter)
specs.drying_method: Vacuum wand using the same vacuum motor as Nitty Gritty's Mini Pro 2 cleaner

products.provenance: Nitty Gritty's manufacturer page describes Model 1.0 as the brand's most inexpensive vacuum-based cleaner, entirely manual (fluid applied, record scrubbed, and platter turned by hand by the operator) but fitted with the identical vacuum motor used in the flagship Mini Pro 2. Elusive Disc corroborates the vinyl wood-grain cabinet, included velvet brush, 4 oz PURE 2 fluid, plastic record turner, 1-year warranty, USA manufacture, and current discounted price of $524 against Nitty Gritty's own $581.99 list. Neither source publishes a motor wattage, cycle duration, or reservoir capacity, so those fields are null.

products.name: Clearaudio Smart Matrix Silent Record Cleaning Machine
products.priceNote: Upscale Audio US retail price; Clearaudio (Germany) sells through a dealer network and does not publish direct consumer pricing

specs.cleaning_method: Vacuum with bi-directional motorized platter rotation and controlled fluid application

products.provenance: Upscale Audio's product page states a maximum power consumption of 300W, $3,200 price, bi-directional automated scrubbing with controlled fluid application and vacuum drying, compatibility with 7", 10", and 12" records, a universal record clamp/adapter, 13.58 x 13.58 x 9.25 in. dimensions, and 23.36 lb weight. Cycle time, tank capacity, and noise level in dB are not stated on the page despite the "Silent" name, so those fields are left null rather than estimated.

products.name: Degritter Mark II Ultrasonic Record Cleaning Machine

specs.cleaning_method: Ultrasonic cavitation (Power Drive 2.0 with Pulse Mode)
specs.drying_method: Filtered-air fan drying, 20 adjustable fan power settings

products.provenance: Music Direct lists $3,600 price and a removable 1.3 L tank with 100 ml cleaning fluid, filters, and 2-year warranty; a review aggregation (Analog Planet) independently confirms two 0.37-gal (1.4 L) tanks. Degritter's own site confirms 120-125 kHz frequency sweep ultrasonic cleaning ("Power Drive 2.0"), up to 300W average power output across programs, 4 total transducers (2 per side), Pulse Mode, active filtration, automatic temperature-controlled cooling, and filtered-air variable-speed fan drying, plus AC 100-240V/4A input, 14.6 x 11 x 8.3 in. dimensions, 19.2 lb weight, and a stated 70 dB noise level. Cycle time is presented as a range of selectable programs rather than one fixed duration in the sourced material, so it is left null rather than picking one figure arbitrarily.

products.name: Spin-Clean Record Washer MKII Complete Kit
products.priceNote: Acoustic Sounds current retail price for the Complete Kit

specs.cleaning_method: Manual immersion/bath wash with dual velvet brushes (non-electric)
specs.tank_capacity: Bath basin; included fluid concentrate rated to clean over 700 records
specs.drying_method: Air-dry using included washable microfiber drying cloths (manual towel-dry, no vacuum or fan)

products.provenance: Acoustic Sounds' listing confirms the $124.99 Complete Kit price for the patented MKII bath-type washer: record washer with lid, 4 oz and 32 oz cleaning-concentrate bottles, 2 pairs of MKII washer brushes, 1 pair of MKII rollers, and 7 washable drying cloths, plus the claim that the included concentrate cleans over 700 records at under a penny per record. The device requires no electricity (motor_power_w set to 0, the device's own documented state, rather than treated as an unknown null), is compatible with 45s/LPs/78s, and uses a biodegradable, phosphate-free formula. No numeric tank volume in liters/oz was published, so tank_capacity is described qualitatively instead of guessed.

products.name: Kirmuss Audio KA-RC-1 Ultrasonic Record Restoration System
products.priceNote: Kirmuss Audio list/MAP price, 120VAC US model

specs.cleaning_method: Ultrasonic cavitation with patented record suspension system
specs.drying_method: Air-dry; residual moisture removed with included lint-free optician's microfiber cloth

products.provenance: Kirmuss Audio's own product page states the $1,490 US list/MAP price, a 6-liter tank, a patented record suspension system holding up to four records simultaneously ("two 33 1/3, one 45, and one 78"), 35 kHz primary ultrasonic frequency with 70 kHz passive resonance, 2-to-5-minute cycles (5-minute final cycle), ETL/CE safety approval, and post-clean drying via an included lint-free microfiber cloth rather than a built-in fan or vacuum. Kirmuss markets this as a groove-level restoration system rather than surface cleaning alone; motor wattage and a dB noise figure are not published, so both are null.

products.provenance: Turntable Lab's listing confirms $349.95 for the current Carbon Fiber/aluminum-top 20th-anniversary edition, 12.56 x 9.93 x 7.12 in. dimensions, 11.5 lb weight, an included 8 oz bottle of RxLP cleaning fluid, manual record turner, record platter, and fluid applicator brush, and a stated capacity of "up to 100 LPs per day." recorddoctor.com, the brand's historical direct domain, now redirects to a domain-parking service, so Turntable Lab is used as the authoritative current source rather than the dead manufacturer link. products.name: Audio Desk Systeme Vinyl Cleaner Premium (Pro) Ultrasonic Record Cleaning Machine
products.priceNote: Music Direct US retail price, drop-shipped from manufacturer (Germany); Audio Desk Systeme does not publish direct consumer pricing

specs.cleaning_method: Fully automatic ultrasonic cleaning with counter-rotating microfiber wet-cleaning barrels on both record sides
specs.cycle_time: 3-minute automated wash-and-dry cycle (reduced from a prior 5-minute cycle on earlier revisions)
specs.drying_method: Integrated high-performance fan drying with static elimination

Ultrasonic frequency in kHz and tank capacity in liters are not published on this page or corroborated elsewhere in this pass, so both are left null rather than carried over from an unverified prior-generation figure.

products.name: iSonic P4875 7.5L Commercial Ultrasonic Cleaner (used for vinyl record cleaning)

specs.cleaning_method: Ultrasonic cavitation (general-purpose commercial tank cleaner adapted for vinyl via separately-sold record racks/mandrels)
specs.cycle_time: Adjustable digital timer, up to 30 minutes, with memory recall
specs.tank_capacity: 7.5 L (2 gal) tank, 6 L (1.6 gal) max operating level
specs.drying_method: None built in; air-dry after removal from the ultrasonic bath

products.provenance: iSonic's own product page states $779.95 price, a 7.5 L (2 gal) total / 6 L (1.6 gal) max-fill stainless tank (13 x 9.4 x 4.1 in. internal), three industrial-grade stack transducers, 35,000 Hz (35 kHz) operating frequency, 140W ultrasonic power (plus a separate 240W heater at 100-120V, or 165W+240W at 220-240V), three selectable heater temperatures, and a digital timer adjustable up to 30 minutes with memory recall. This is a general-purpose commercial ultrasonic cleaning tank, not a vinyl-specific appliance — it lacks a built-in drying stage or a fixed "records per cycle" rack, since capacity depends on the separately-sold vinyl-holder accessory a buyer pairs with it, so records_per_cycle and noise_level_db are left null rather than assumed.

products.name: GEM Dandy Hydraulic LP Cleaning Apparatus Mk II
products.priceNote: Price as documented in a detailed 6moons product review of the current Mk II unit; HiFi GEM's own current product page does not display a list price, so this may not reflect present-day pricing

specs.cleaning_method: No-contact hydraulic wash: tap-water jet flushes the groove at an angle while the LP rotates on a protected mandrel
specs.drying_method: Manual towel-dry with a soft cloth after rinsing (no vacuum, fan, or heater)

products.provenance: CORRECTED/CLARIFIED FROM SEED: "Gem Dandy" is not a vacuum or ultrasonic RCM but a distinct no-contact hydraulic (pressurized tap-water jet) cleaning apparatus invented by George E. Merrill, still manufactured today by HiFi GEM as the Hydraulic LP Cleaning Apparatus Mk II (label-protecting rotating mandrel, faucet-fed water jet at an angle, no brushes or vacuum). HiFi GEM's own current page confirms the Mk II revision (o-ring seals, hand wheel, new bearing, stainless components per the Australian distributor GrooveWorks) and that it ships with a mandrel stand, jet hose, cleaning solution, and lubricant, but does not list a price. A detailed 6moons review of the current product documents a $119 apparatus price (plus $9 cleaning solution, $24 lube kit), the tap-water-jet mechanism at roughly 60-70°F water temperature and a 30° rotation angle, and a manual-cloth drying step — used here as the price source since it is a directly-published figure rather than an estimate, flagged in priceNote as possibly dated. The device draws no electrical power (motor_power_w = 0, its documented state) and has no numeric tank, cycle-time, frequency, or dB specification to report.

products.name: Moth Mk2 Record Cleaning Machine (discontinued; secondhand market only)
products.priceNote: No current manufacturer or authorized-dealer listing found; UK hi-fi forum secondhand asking prices seen around GBP 275-280 (approx. late-2020s market, not a fixed USD MSRP) — left null rather than converting a fluctuating used-market price into a guessed USD figure
products.provenance: CORRECTED FROM SEED: the Moth Mk2 is a UK-made vacuum RCM, sold historically either factory-built or as a DIY kit, but no current manufacturer storefront or active product page could be found in this research pass — every reachable reference (a used-audio forum sale thread on theartofsound.net asking GBP 280, a second forum listing at GBP 275, and a vintage-audio retailer page (retrotechaudio.co.uk) selling a used, fully working unit with accessories) treats it strictly as a secondhand/collector item today. Unlike the analogous Wilton->JET bench-grinder correction, no verifiable current-production successor or rebrand could be confirmed live, so this entry is retained as a legacy product with priceUsd left null and cleaning-method/drying-method specified generically as a vacuum RCM based on the corroborating listings, rather than inventing numeric specs no live source actually published.
